unit.title: Fractions
unit.blurb: Equivalent fractions and ordering, adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers, multiplying and dividing fractions by whole numbers, and shortcuts.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Use equivalent fractions to compare and order fractions, including improper fractions and mixed numbers.

O2.t: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with different denominators.

O3.t: Multiply a fraction by a whole number and by another fraction, and find fractions of amounts.

O4.t: Divide a proper fraction by a whole number.

O5.t: Use the laws of arithmetic and simplifying to make fraction calculations easier.

p: In class A, **7/10** of students passed a swimming test. In class B, **5/8** passed. In class C, **2/3** passed.
Which class had the greatest fraction passing? Try it before you read on.
Multiply (or divide) the numerator and denominator by the same number: 2/3 = 4/6 = 8/12.

qq.hint: 5 × 4 = 20, so multiply the top by 4 too.

p: To compare fractions, write them with the **same denominator** – then the larger numerator is the larger fraction.
p2: 120 is the lowest common multiple of 10, 8 and 3. Order, largest first: **7/10, 2/3, 5/8** – class A did best.
Converting to **decimals** (divide numerator by denominator) also works; some decimals go on forever, like 2/3 = 0.666…

p: An **improper fraction** has a numerator bigger than its denominator: 11/4. As a **mixed number** that is 2 3/4 (11 ÷ 4 = 2 r 3).
To compare 2 3/4 and 13/5: compare whole parts first – 13/5 = 2 3/5. Both have 2 wholes; 3/4 = 15/20 > 3/5 = 12/20, so **2 3/4 > 13/5**.
Step 1: Change any improper fractions to mixed numbers; compare whole-number parts first.
Step 2: Find a common denominator (the LCM of the denominators).
Step 3: Write equivalent fractions and compare the numerators – or convert to decimals.
Step 4: Write the ORIGINAL fractions in the order asked for.

p: A cake recipe needs **2 1/4 cups** of flour and the icing needs **1 2/3 cups**.
How much flour is that altogether? Is it more or less than 4 cups? Try it before you read on.
1/4 + 2/3 = 3/12 + 8/12 = 11/12. Add the numerators only – the denominator tells the size of the pieces.

errs.fb: Don't add the denominators – use a common denominator.

p: **Step 1:** Add the whole numbers (this is also a good estimate). **Step 2:** Add the fractions using a common denominator. **Step 3:** If the fraction part is improper, change it to a mixed number and add it on.
p2: So **3 11/12 cups** – a little less than 4.

p: Subtracting: 5 1/3 − 2 3/4. The fraction 1/3 is smaller than 3/4, so it's easiest to use improper fractions: 16/3 − 11/4 = 64/12 − 33/12 = 31/12 = **2 7/12**.

lesson.t: How do I add or subtract mixed numbers?
p: Step 1: Estimate with the whole numbers.
Step 2: Add (or subtract) the whole numbers.
Step 3: Add (or subtract) the fractions using a common denominator; simplify.
Step 4: If a fraction is improper, carry the whole; if you can't subtract, use improper fractions. Compare with the estimate.

captions: A cake recipe needs 2 and a quarter cups of flour.
The icing needs 1 and 2 thirds cups.
Altogether, is that more or less than 4 cups?
Pause the video and decide.
The whole numbers make 3.
Then we have a quarter and 2 thirds left to add.
A quarter plus 2 thirds is 11 twelfths.
That is less than 1 whole.
So the total is 3 and 11 twelfths cups: just less than 4.
Remember: to add fractions, they need a common denominator.
Thirds and quarters can both be written as twelfths.
Add the numerators only.
The denominator tells you the size of the pieces, and that does not change.
To add mixed numbers, add the whole numbers first.
This also gives you a good estimate.
Then add the fractions, using a common denominator.
If the fraction part is improper, change it to a mixed number, and add it on.
For example, 1 and 3 quarters plus 2 and a half.
The wholes make 3.
3 quarters plus 2 quarters is 5 quarters, which is 1 and a quarter.
So the total is 4 and a quarter.
Your turn.
Work out 1 and 1 fifth, plus 2 and 2 fifths.
Pause the video and try it.
1 plus 2 is 3.
1 fifth plus 2 fifths is 3 fifths.
The answer is 3 and 3 fifths.
Subtracting can be tricky.
Take 5 and 1 third, minus 2 and 3 quarters.
1 third is smaller than 3 quarters, so we cannot just subtract the fractions.
The safest method is to change both numbers to improper fractions.
5 and 1 third is 16 thirds.
2 and 3 quarters is 11 quarters.
In twelfths, that is 64 twelfths minus 33 twelfths, which is 31 twelfths.
As a mixed number, 2 and 7 twelfths.
Here is the method.
Step 1: estimate with the whole numbers.
Step 2: add or subtract the whole numbers.
Step 3: add or subtract the fractions with a common denominator, and simplify.
Step 4: if a fraction is improper, carry.
For a hard subtraction, use improper fractions.
Work out 1 and 5 eighths, plus 3 and 3 quarters.
The wholes: 1 plus 3 is 4.
The fractions: 5 eighths plus 6 eighths is 11 eighths.
That is 1 and 3 eighths.
4 plus 1 and 3 eighths is 5 and 3 eighths.
Your turn.
Work out 2 and 3 quarters, plus 1 and a half.
Pause and work it out.
The wholes make 3.
3 quarters plus 2 quarters is 5 quarters, which is 1 and a quarter.
3 plus 1 and a quarter is 4 and a quarter.
Work out 6 and 2 fifths, minus 3 and a half.
Change to improper fractions.
6 and 2 fifths is 32 fifths.
3 and a half is 7 halves.
In tenths: 64 tenths minus 35 tenths is 29 tenths.
That is 2 and 9 tenths.
Lin works out 1 and 1 third, plus 2 and a quarter.
Which line goes wrong first?
Line 2 is wrong.
You cannot add the tops and add the bottoms.
Thirds and quarters are different sizes.
Use twelfths.
4 twelfths plus 3 twelfths is 7 twelfths.
The answer is 3 and 7 twelfths.
Cooks add mixed numbers all the time.
Suppose a recipe needs 1 and a half cups of milk, and you want to make it three times.
1 and a half plus 1 and a half is 3.
Add another 1 and a half, and you get 4 and a half cups.
A measuring jug marked in halves, thirds and quarters is really a fraction number line.
One last question.
What is 3 minus 1 and 1 third?
Pause the video and answer.
3 is 9 thirds.
1 and 1 third is 4 thirds.
9 thirds minus 4 thirds is 5 thirds, which is 1 and 2 thirds.
To remember: add the wholes, then add the fractions with a common denominator.
Change an improper fraction part to a mixed number, and carry.
For subtraction, improper fractions avoid problems.
Estimate with the whole numbers, and simplify your answer.

p: **3/4** of a garden is lawn. A gardener mows **2/3** of the lawn before it rains.
What fraction of the whole garden has been mown? Try it before you read on.
To find 3/5 of 40: divide by the denominator, multiply by the numerator: 40 ÷ 5 × 3 = 24.
2/3 **of** 3/4 is the same as **2/3 × 3/4**. A diagram shows why: split a rectangle into 4 columns and shade 3 (that's 3/4); split it into 3 rows and take 2 of them.
p2: 6 of the 12 small squares are in both: 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = **1/2**. Half the garden has been mown.
**Rule:** multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators: (2 × 3)/(3 × 4) = 6/12 = 1/2.

p: You can simplify **before** multiplying by dividing a numerator and a denominator by a common factor: 2/3 × 3/4 → cancel the threes, and 2 with 4 → 1/1 × 1/2 = 1/2.
A whole number is a fraction over 1: 5 × 2/3 = 5/1 × 2/3 = 10/3 = **3 1/3**.
Multiplying by a proper fraction makes the answer **smaller**.

p: Step 1: Write any whole number as a fraction over 1 (and mixed numbers as improper fractions).

captions: 3 quarters of a garden is lawn.
A gardener mows 2 thirds of the lawn before it starts to rain.
What fraction of the whole garden has been mown?
Pause the video and work it out.
Draw the garden as a rectangle with 4 columns.
3 of the columns are lawn.
That is 3 quarters.
Now cut it into 3 rows, and take 2 of them.
The dark part has been mown.
There are 12 small pieces, and 6 are dark.
6 twelfths is one half.
Half of the garden has been mown.
Remember how to find a fraction of an amount.
For 3 fifths of 40, divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.
40 divided by 5 is 8.
8 times 3 is 24.
2 thirds of 3 quarters is the same as 2 thirds times 3 quarters.
To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators, and multiply the denominators.
2 times 3 is 6.
3 times 4 is 12.
That gives 6 twelfths, which simplifies to one half.
It matches the diagram.
Your turn.
Work out 1 third times 1 quarter.
Pause the video and try it.
1 times 1 is 1.
3 times 4 is 12.
The answer is 1 twelfth.
You can make the numbers smaller before you multiply.
This is called cancelling.
Divide a numerator and a denominator by the same number.
In 2 thirds times 3 quarters, the threes cancel.
And 2 and 4 both divide by 2.
That leaves 1 over 1, times 1 over 2, which is one half.
A whole number can be written as a fraction over 1.
So 5 times 2 thirds is 5 over 1, times 2 over 3.
That is 10 thirds, or 3 and 1 third.
Here is the method.
Step 1: write any whole number as a fraction over 1.
Step 2: cancel common factors between any numerator and any denominator.
Step 3: multiply the numerators, and multiply the denominators.
Step 4: simplify, and change an improper fraction to a mixed number.
Work out 4 ninths times 3 eighths.
Cancel 4 with 8.
They become 1 and 2.
Cancel 3 with 9.
They become 1 and 3.
1 third times 1 half is 1 sixth.
Work out 6 times 5 eighths.
Write 6 as 6 over 1.
Cancel 6 and 8 by 2.
They become 3 and 4.
3 times 5 is 15.
1 times 4 is 4.
15 quarters is 3 and 3 quarters.
Your turn.
Work out 4 times 3 tenths.
Pause and work it out.
4 times 3 is 12, so we get 12 tenths.
That simplifies to 6 fifths, which is 1 and 1 fifth.
In a club, 3 fifths of the members are adults.
5 sixths of the adults play tennis.
What fraction of the club are adults who play tennis?
We need 5 sixths of 3 fifths.
Of means multiply.
The fives cancel.
3 and 6 cancel to 1 and 2.
The answer is one half.
Half of the club are adults who play tennis.
Omar works out 2 fifths times 3 quarters.
Which line is wrong?
Line 1 is wrong.
Omar multiplied across the wrong way.
Multiply top by top, and bottom by bottom.
2 times 3 is 6, and 5 times 4 is 20.
6 twentieths simplifies to 3 tenths.
Here is a real fraction of a fraction.
About 7 tenths of the Earth's surface is covered by water.
And the Pacific Ocean holds roughly half of all that water surface.
One half times 7 tenths is 7 twentieths.
So the Pacific Ocean alone covers about a third of the whole planet.
One last question.
Is 3 quarters times 4 fifths more than 3 quarters, or less?
Pause the video and choose.
It is less than 3 quarters.
Multiplying by a fraction smaller than 1 makes the answer smaller.
In fact, the fours cancel, and the answer is 3 fifths.
To remember: of means multiply.
Multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators, and simplify.
Cancel common factors first, to make it easier.
A whole number is a fraction over 1.
And multiplying by a proper fraction makes the answer smaller.
Great work! Now practise lesson 7.3 on Camday.

p: There is **3/4** of a pizza left. Three friends share it equally.
What fraction of a whole pizza does each friend get? And how many 1/8 slices are in the 3/4? Try it before you read on.
12 ÷ 3 asks 'how many 3s are in 12?' – 4. It also means 'share 12 into 3 equal groups'.

errs.fb: That is 5 shared into 2. How many halves fit in 5?

p: Sharing 3/4 between 3 people: 3 quarters shared by 3 is **1/4** each.
In general, dividing by 3 is the same as finding 1/3: 3/4 ÷ 3 = 3/4 × 1/3 = 3/12 = **1/4**.
3/4 ÷ 1/8 asks: how many eighths are in 3/4? 3/4 = 6/8, so there are **6**.
Method: turn the second fraction upside down (its **reciprocal**) and multiply: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 3/4 × 8/1 = 24/4 = 6.

Step 2: Keep the first fraction; change ÷ to ×; flip the second fraction (reciprocal).
Step 3: Cancel and multiply.
Step 4: Check: does the size make sense? ÷ a whole number makes it smaller; ÷ a proper fraction makes it bigger.

Keep the first fraction; flip only the second.

captions: There is 3 quarters of a pizza left.
Three friends share it equally.
What fraction of a whole pizza does each friend get?
Pause the video and work it out.
3 quarters means 3 pieces, each a quarter of the pizza.
Three friends, three pieces.
They get one quarter each.
Remember: 12 divided by 3 can mean share 12 into 3 equal groups.
It can also mean: how many threes are in 12?
Both give 4.
The second meaning helps with fractions.
How many halves are in 5?
There are 10.
Dividing by 3 is the same as finding one third.
So dividing by 3 is the same as multiplying by 1 third.
3 quarters divided by 3 is 3 quarters times 1 third.
That is 3 twelfths, which simplifies to 1 quarter.
Another example.
2 fifths divided by 4 is 2 fifths times 1 quarter.
That is 2 twentieths, or 1 tenth.
Your turn.
Work out 8 ninths divided by 4.
Pause the video and try it.
8 ninths shared into 4 equal parts is 2 ninths each.
Or: 8 ninths times 1 quarter is 8 over 36, which simplifies to 2 ninths.
3 quarters divided by 1 eighth asks: how many eighths are in 3 quarters?
3 quarters is the same as 6 eighths.
So there are 6.
Here is the method.
Turn the second fraction upside down, and multiply.
The upside-down fraction is called the reciprocal.
3 quarters times 8 over 1 is 24 quarters, which is 6.
The same answer.
Here is the method.
Step 1: write a whole number as a fraction over 1.
Step 2: keep the first fraction.
Change divide to multiply.
Flip the second fraction.
Step 3: cancel, and multiply.
Step 4: check that the size of your answer makes sense.
Work out 2 thirds divided by 4 ninths.
Keep the first, change to times, flip the second.
2 thirds times 9 quarters.
Cancel 2 with 4, to get 1 and 2.
Cancel 3 with 9, to get 1 and 3.
That gives 3 halves, which is 1 and a half.
Your turn.
How many sixths are in 2 thirds?
Pause and work it out.
2 thirds divided by 1 sixth is 2 thirds times 6.
That is 12 thirds, which is 4.
There are 4 sixths in 2 thirds.
A bottle holds 5 sixths of a litre.
How many doses of 1 twelfth of a litre can be poured from it?
5 sixths times 12 over 1 is 60 sixths.
60 divided by 6 is 10.
You can pour 10 doses.
A ribbon is 3 fifths of a metre long.
It is cut into 4 equal pieces.
How long is each piece?
Dividing by 4 is multiplying by 1 quarter.
3 fifths times 1 quarter is 3 twentieths of a metre.
3 twentieths of a metre is 15 centimetres.
Jay works out 2 fifths divided by 3 quarters.
Which line is wrong?
Line 1 is wrong.
Jay flipped the first fraction.
Keep the first fraction, and flip only the second.
2 fifths times 4 thirds is 8 fifteenths.
Musicians divide fractions without even noticing.
A waltz is written in 3 4 time.
Each bar lasts 3 quarter notes.
How many eighth notes fit in one bar?
That is 3 quarters divided by 1 eighth.
3 quarters times 8 is 6.
So 6 eighth notes fit in every bar of a waltz.
One last question.
What is 1 half divided by 1 quarter?
Pause the video and answer.
How many quarters are in a half?
Or: 1 half times 4 is 4 halves, which is 2.
To remember: dividing by a whole number n is multiplying by 1 over n.
To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal.
Keep the first fraction, and flip only the second.
Dividing by a proper fraction gives a bigger answer.

lesson.t: How do I make a fraction calculation easier?
p: Step 1: Look at the fraction: close to 1? Use 'whole − small part'.
Step 2: Look for common factors: cancel before you multiply.
Step 3: Split a denominator into factors, or re-order the multiplication.
Step 4: Remember the order of operations; check with an estimate.

captions: A games console costs 480 dollars.
In a sale, it is 5 sixths of the usual price.
What is the sale price?
Try to find a quick way.
Pause the video and work it out.
5 sixths is the whole price, minus 1 sixth.
And 1 sixth of 480 is easy: it is 80.
480 minus 80 is 400.
The sale price is 400 dollars.
Remember factors.
The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
A number can be split into factors in different ways.
24 is 4 times 6, and also 3 times 8.
When a fraction is close to 1, find the small missing part, and subtract it from the whole.
9 tenths of 350.
1 tenth is 35.
So 9 tenths is 350 minus 35, which is 315.
3 quarters of 96.
1 quarter is 24.
So 3 quarters is 96 minus 24, which is 72.
Your turn.
Work out 4 fifths of 650.
Pause the video and try it.
1 fifth of 650 is 130.
Take that away from 650.
The answer is 520.
Here are three more ideas.
First: use factors.
1 twelfth is 1 third of 1 quarter.
So 1 twelfth of 600 is 1 third of 150, which is 50.
Second: cancel before you multiply.
In 15 over 28, times 14 over 45: 14 and 28 share a factor of 14, and 15 and 45 share a factor of 15.
That leaves 1 half times 1 third, which is 1 sixth.
Third: re-order.
In 3 sevenths times 5 times 14, do 3 sevenths of 14 first.
That is 6.
Then 6 times 5 is 30.
Here is the method.
Step 1: look at the fraction.
Is it close to 1?
Then use whole minus the small part.
Step 2: look for common factors, and cancel before you multiply.
Step 3: split a denominator into factors, or re-order the multiplication.
Step 4: follow the order of operations.
Multiply and divide before you add and subtract.
Work out 11 twelfths of 840.
1 twelfth of 840 is 70.
840 minus 70 is 770.
Work out 1 fifteenth of 2,400.
15 is 3 times 5.
So find 1 fifth first, then 1 third of that.
1 fifth of 2,400 is 480.
1 third of 480 is 160.
Your turn.
Work out 1 twentieth of 1,800.
Pause and work it out.
20 is 10 times 2.
1 tenth of 1,800 is 180.
Half of 180 is 90.
Work out 18 over 25, times 35 over 36.
Cancel 18 and 36.
They become 1 and 2.
Cancel 35 and 25.
They become 7 and 5.
1 fifth times 7 halves is 7 tenths.
Work out 2 thirds, plus 1 third times 3 quarters.
Multiply first.
1 third times 3 quarters is 1 quarter.
Then add.
2 thirds plus 1 quarter is 8 twelfths plus 3 twelfths, which is 11 twelfths.
Ana works out 1 half, plus 1 half times 1 half.
Which line is wrong?
Line 1 is wrong.
Ana added first.
You must multiply before you add.
1 half times 1 half is 1 quarter.
Then 1 half plus 1 quarter is 3 quarters.
You can use these tricks in any shop.
A sign says 10 percent off.
That means you pay 9 tenths of the price.
A pair of trainers costs 70 dollars.
1 tenth is 7 dollars.
70 minus 7 is 63.
You pay 63 dollars.
No written calculation needed.
One last question.
Work out 1 third, plus 2 thirds times 1 half.
Pause the video and answer.
Multiply first.
2 thirds times 1 half is 1 third.
Then 1 third plus 1 third is 2 thirds.
To remember: for a fraction close to 1, use the whole minus the small part.
Split denominators into factors.
1 twelfth is 1 third of 1 quarter.
Cancel before multiplying, and re-order when it helps.
And always follow the order of operations.
